findings.summary: Discrete-time piecewise-smooth systems can change invariant sets when trajectories cross a switching surface. Border-collision theory therefore supplies an ordinary explanation for durable post-Top-k divergence: boundary crossing can move the system into a different basin/attractor, not merely create an immediate jump.
sources: Simpson, Border-Collision Bifurcations in R^N, SIAM Review 58(2), 2016, DOI 10.1137/15M1006982
Simpson, Border-collision bifurcations from stable fixed points to any number of coexisting chaotic attractors, arXiv:2207.10251, 2022

findings.summary: Recurrent lateral-inhibition/WTA networks can have multiple stable equilibria and hysteretic state transitions. A small routing perturbation can therefore produce persistent post-perturbation differences through ordinary attractor selection/hysteresis.
sources: Mao & Massaquoi, Dynamics of winner-take-all competition in recurrent neural networks with lateral inhibition, IEEE TNN 18(1), 2007, DOI 10.1109/TNN.2006.883724
Cotteret et al., Robust Spiking Attractor Networks with a Hard Winner-Take-All Neuron Circuit, ISCAS 2023, DOI 10.1109/ISCAS46773.2023.10181513

findings.summary: Piecewise-contracting systems can still exhibit nontrivial recurrent/chaotic attractors when discontinuities participate in the attractor. Consequently a locally stable or contractive within-region Jacobian does not by itself rule out switching-driven long-lived complexity.
sources: Catsigeras, Guiraud, Meyroneinc & Ugalde, On the asymptotic properties of piecewise contracting maps, Dynamical Systems 31(2), 2016, DOI 10.1080/14689367.2015.1068274
